description: Machine learning methods for clinical data and the specific ways that health data defeats naive modelling: missing and biased records, irregular signals, causal questions, subgroup harm and dataset shift. Students build and evaluate clinical risk models, signal and text pipelines and causal analyses in notebooks, then judge regulation and deployment in Ghanaian and wider African health settings.
modelledOn: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning
Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If
WHO guidance on ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health
outcomes: Prepare clinical records for modelling, naming the sources of missingness, bias and label error and choosing sound cohort definitions.
Build and evaluate risk and survival models with discrimination, calibration and decision-curve analysis on a time-respecting split.
Process physiological signals, medical images and clinical text with appropriate models and judge their failure modes.
Estimate treatment effects from observational data using propensity, doubly robust and target-trial approaches, and state the assumptions required.
Audit a model for subgroup performance, dataset shift and uncertainty, and design monitoring for it after deployment.
Assess a clinical AI product against regulatory, validation and ethical requirements and plan its deployment in a low-resource health system.

units.title: Clinical data and its quirks
topics: Sources and structure: electronic records, registries, claims and device data; FHIR resources and standard vocabularies (ICD, SNOMED CT, LOINC)
Defining cohorts, outcomes and index times; computable phenotypes
Missing data: MCAR, MAR and informative missingness; imputation and missingness indicators
Irregular sampling, measurement bias and why a lab test being ordered is itself a signal
Selection and time-related biases: immortal time, leakage and look-ahead
Privacy and governance: de-identification, consent, and the Ghana Data Protection Act

units.title: Risk stratification and prediction
topics: Supervised models for clinical risk: regularised logistic regression, gradient boosting and sparse score cards
Time-to-event modelling: Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression and censoring
Discrimination: ROC and precision-recall analysis, and their dependence on prevalence
Calibration: reliability curves, calibration slope and recalibration
Decision-curve analysis and net benefit; choosing thresholds from clinical cost
Study design: temporal and site-wise splits, sample size and overfitting; imbalance handling
Early warning scores and maternal-risk triage tools used in low-resource clinics

units.title: Physiological time series
topics: ECG, photoplethysmography and EEG: acquisition, noise sources and filtering
QRS detection and heart-rate variability features
Irregular ICU and ward vital-sign series: alignment, imputation and windowing
Sequence models: one-dimensional convolutions, recurrent networks and transformers for signals
Hidden Markov and state-space models for physiological state tracking
Alarm fatigue, anomaly detection and low-cost wearable sensing in rural settings

units.title: Medical images
topics: Convolutional networks for chest X-ray and retinal image classification; transfer learning
Segmentation with encoder-decoder networks and Dice overlap
Label scarcity, weak labels and annotation disagreement between clinicians
Explanation by saliency maps and its limits
Screening deployments: tuberculosis radiology and diabetic retinopathy in district hospitals

units.title: Clinical text and language models
topics: Clinical text properties: abbreviations, negation, templates and copy-paste
Named-entity recognition, negation and temporal relations; automatic ICD coding
Word embeddings and transformer encoders pre-trained on clinical text
Large language models for summarisation and question answering; hallucination and safety evaluation
Low-resource languages and code-switching: Twi, Ewe and Hausa in health communication
Evaluating text models: reader studies, error taxonomies and privacy leakage

units.title: Causal inference with observational data
topics: Potential outcomes, confounding and directed acyclic graphs; adjustment sets
Propensity scores: matching, weighting and overlap diagnostics
Doubly robust estimation and targeted learning
Target-trial emulation and guarding against immortal-time and selection bias
Instrumental variables, regression discontinuity and difference-in-differences
Heterogeneous treatment effects: meta-learners and causal forests
Treatment policies and off-policy evaluation; reinforcement learning for sepsis and dosing, and its risks

units.title: Fairness, robustness and dataset shift
topics: Subgroup performance and fairness criteria: equalised odds, calibration within groups, and their incompatibility
Sources of bias: label proxies, unequal access to care and under-represented populations
Covariate, label and concept shift; temporal drift and site transfer
Detecting shift and monitoring model performance without labels
Uncertainty quantification and conformal prediction; deferral to clinicians
Interpretable and explainable models in clinical practice

units.title: Regulation, validation and deployment
topics: Software as a medical device: risk classes, regulators and the Ghana Food and Drugs Authority position
Validation ladder: retrospective, silent-mode and prospective studies; reporting guidelines for prediction models and AI trials
Workflow integration, human factors and alert fatigue
Monitoring and updating deployed models; change control
Privacy-preserving learning: federated learning and differential privacy across hospitals
Ethics, accountability and consent; liability when a model errs
Project: a clinical prediction study, from cohort definition to a deployment and monitoring plan

schedule.title: Clinical data sources and cohorts
schedule.exercise: Define a cohort, index time and outcome for 30-day readmission from a described record system, and say which codes and tests you would use for the phenotype.

tasks.title: Parse a FHIR-style JSON bundle of patient records into a table of encounters, diagnoses and lab results, and report counts per resource type
Build a cohort from synthetic visit records using inclusion, exclusion and index-date rules, and draw the attrition counts at each step
Compare mean imputation, multiple imputation and missingness indicators on a lab dataset with informative missingness, and report the effect on a model's AUROC

schedule.title: Bias, leakage and privacy
schedule.exercise: Find three leakage or bias problems in a described study design, and write the de-identification steps needed to share a clinic dataset under Ghana law.

tasks.title: Show that lab test ordering predicts the outcome independent of the result, and quantify its effect on a risk model on synthetic data
Find and remove the leaking features and immortal-time errors from a given feature table, and report how performance changes after correction
Prepare a clinic dataset for sharing in a case file: choose identifiers to remove, check re-identification risk and justify against the rubric

schedule.title: Building clinical risk models
schedule.exercise: Fit a logistic regression and a gradient-boosted model to predict diabetes complications, plot ROC and precision-recall curves, and fit a Cox model with censored follow-up.

tasks.title: Train a regularised logistic regression on a synthetic clinic dataset and report coefficients as odds ratios with confidence intervals
Estimate Kaplan-Meier survival curves for two treatment groups, with censoring, and compare them with a log-rank test
Compare ROC and precision-recall curves for the same model at 2 percent and 20 percent prevalence, and explain why AUROC barely moves

schedule.title: Calibration, utility and study design
schedule.exercise: Check calibration of a risk score on a new hospital, compute net benefit at three thresholds, and design a temporal validation split for a sepsis model.

tasks.title: Plot a reliability curve for a model, compute calibration slope and intercept, and recalibrate on a new site's data
Compute net benefit across thresholds from 1 to 40 percent and plot a decision curve for the model against treating all and none
Compare a random split with a temporal split on a drifting dataset and measure the optimism of the random split

schedule.title: ECG and signal processing
schedule.exercise: Filter a noisy ECG, detect R peaks, compute heart rate and heart-rate variability, and decide how to window and align ICU vital signs for a model.

tasks.title: Apply a band-pass filter to a noisy ECG and a notch filter for mains noise, and plot the signal before and after
Implement a QRS detector with derivative, squaring and moving-window integration, and measure sensitivity and precision against annotated beats
Resample irregular vital signs to hourly windows with last-value carry-forward and masks, and compare imputation methods by downstream error

schedule.title: Sequence models and monitoring
schedule.exercise: Train a one-dimensional convolutional network on ECG segments, fit a hidden Markov model to vital-sign states, and propose an alarm policy that reduces false alarms.

tasks.title: Step a one-dimensional convolution and a recurrent network over an ECG window in the visualiser, and describe what each layer extracts
Fit a two-state hidden Markov model to heart-rate series from stable and deteriorating patients, and decode the most likely state sequence
Design an alarm rule with persistence and context, replay 48 hours of ward data, and compare alarms per patient-day and missed events

schedule.title: Medical image learning
schedule.exercise: Fine-tune a pre-trained network for chest X-ray triage on a small labelled set, measure inter-reader disagreement, and discuss where a tuberculosis screening tool would fail in a district hospital.

tasks.title: Fine-tune a pre-trained image classifier on 500 labelled X-ray patches and report sensitivity at 90 percent specificity
Compute Dice and intersection-over-union for predicted and reference masks on 20 images, and rank cases by error
Generate saliency maps for correct and wrong predictions, and check whether the highlighted regions match the clinical finding

schedule.title: Clinical text and language models
schedule.exercise: Extract medications and negated findings from ten free-text notes, evaluate a summarisation model for hallucinated facts, and compare performance in English and a local language.

tasks.title: Write a rule-based negation detector for clinical sentences, and measure precision and recall on 100 labelled mentions
Train a text classifier on note embeddings to assign diagnosis codes, and compare it with a bag-of-words baseline on macro F1
Review summaries from a language model against source notes in a case file, mark hallucinations and omissions, and set a safety rule for use

schedule.title: Confounding and propensity methods
schedule.exercise: Draw a DAG for a treatment-outcome question, choose the adjustment set, and compare crude, regression-adjusted, propensity-weighted and doubly robust estimates.

tasks.title: Draw a DAG for the effect of a drug on recovery, list confounders and colliders, and name the minimal adjustment set
Estimate treatment effects by inverse-probability weighting on a synthetic dataset with known truth, and check covariate balance after weighting
Implement a doubly robust estimator, then break the outcome model and then the propensity model, and show when it stays unbiased

schedule.title: Target trials, instruments and treatment policies
schedule.exercise: Emulate a target trial from records with eligibility, time zero and follow-up stated, and explain when an instrument or a difference-in-differences design is credible.

tasks.title: Estimate an effect with an instrumental variable on simulated data with unmeasured confounding and compare it with the naive estimate
Fit a causal forest or meta-learner to find which patients benefit most, and test whether the discovered subgroups hold in held-out data
Walk through a dosing policy evaluated off-policy from logged data, and identify where importance weights explode and the estimate becomes unreliable

schedule.title: Fairness, shift and uncertainty
schedule.exercise: Audit a risk model across age, sex and facility type, test it on a shifted site, and add a conformal prediction layer that defers uncertain cases.

tasks.title: Compute AUROC, calibration and false-negative rate per subgroup for a trained model, and flag the groups with a significant gap
Train on one hospital and test on another, detect covariate shift with a classifier two-sample test, and apply reweighting
Add split conformal prediction to a classifier, check 90 percent coverage on test data, and report the rate of deferrals to clinicians

schedule.title: Regulation and validation
schedule.exercise: Classify a sepsis-alert product as a medical device, list the evidence a regulator would expect, and plan a silent-mode evaluation followed by a prospective study.

tasks.title: Classify an AI triage tool by risk class and list the regulatory evidence required, using a case file and the rubric
Plan a silent-mode pilot of a model in a regional hospital, choose success criteria, and decide go or no-go from interim results
Simulate a deployed model with a rising false-alert rate, build a monitor that detects the drift, and show how late it fires

schedule.title: Privacy-preserving learning, ethics and project
schedule.exercise: Compare central, federated and differentially private training for a multi-hospital model, and present your clinical prediction study with its validation and monitoring plan.

tasks.title: Train a model across three simulated hospitals with federated averaging, and compare it with pooled and single-site models on accuracy
Add noise for differential privacy to a trained model's statistics and plot accuracy against the privacy budget
Decide accountability and consent in a case where a deployed model contributes to a missed diagnosis, and defend the position against the rubric
